title: Repair a verification script
description: The script for a claim did not work (an error, a rule of the sandbox, no values reported). The model sees the claim, the data description, the script and the problem and returns a corrected script.

guide.default:
Write a short Python script. It has these names: `data` (the input, parsed JSON; read it, never retype, reassign or change it) and, only if web access was granted, `web` (`web.get(url)` returns the page text, `web.search(query)` returns results).
Allowed imports: math, statistics, fractions, decimal, datetime, calendar, re, json, itertools, collections, string, functools, operator, heapq, bisect, textwrap, unicodedata, csv, base64, hashlib, html, urllib.parse, typing, copy, numbers, enum. There is no file access, no network, no other module. The script must set `result` to JSON data. For a check, `result` is
{"holds": true or false, "values": {the numbers and facts the script used}, "explanation": "one sentence"}. Print nothing else that matters.

body.system: You repair short Python scripts that check claims by recomputing them from the given data. You never trust the claim; you only use what the guide allows.

origin.note: tried with the real model; no harness measurements yet
